classification.difficultyReason: Calculate a z-score and interpret an extreme value to evaluate a contextual claim.

content.prompt: A machine fills packets of lollies. The mean number of lollies in each packet is 40 with a standard deviation of 1.5 lollies. The number of lollies is normally distributed. Rory claims that he bought a packet that had 48 lollies in it. Discuss Rory’s claim.

answer.short: $z\approx5.33$. Rory’s claim is extremely unlikely, although it is possible under the normal model.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}z&=\frac{48-40}{1.5}\\&=\frac{16}{3}\\&\approx5.33\end{aligned}$$
A packet containing 48 lollies is more than five standard deviations above the mean. The empirical rule places approximately 99.7% of values within three standard deviations, so Rory’s claim is extremely unlikely, although it is possible under the normal model.
